# Operation coverage

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_ops.py from ops.toml. Do not edit. -->

46 of 47 operations can run on the device. Everything else reaches
PyTorch's CPU implementation through the fallback, which is correct and costs two
transfers.

How an operation runs depends on its category. An elementwise one is an expression the
emitter drops into a shared loop, so it fuses with its neighbours. A reduction reads a
whole axis to write one element, which needs a kernel of its own. A movement operation
rearranges indices and computes nothing: the device runs it as a view, so it has no
kernel at all, and partitioning leaves one on the host unless it sits beside work that
earns the transfer.

This counts operations rather than a graph. `tools/model_coverage.py` counts a real one,
and the two numbers are far apart.
